title: BANZARE survey theodolite
dateKind: The expedition’s documented use of the instrument.
summary: SPRI identifies this surveying instrument as made by Carl Zeiss in Jena. Its body is marked 16166. The catalogue associates this instrument with BANZARE, the British Australian and New Zealand Antarctic Research Expedition.
limits: The engraved number identifies this instrument. It does not, alone, establish when it was set up or what readings were recorded.
alt: A pale horizontal telescope sits above a circular scale and square dark foot.

title: Case and tools for the BANZARE theodolite
dateKind: The associated Antarctic research expedition dated in the catalogue.
summary: The record identifies this case as the companion of N: 115a. The box holds named fittings, including a brush, spanner, compass and spare light equipment. The entry itself links it to the instrument numbered 16166.
limits: The catalogue links case and instrument directly. It does not say the number 16166 is engraved on the outside of this box.
alt: A hinged low wooden chest with metal catches and a separate strip for fittings.

title: Swift microscope body 16616
dateKind: The body has a serial number. The collection entry gives no making date.
summary: The black monocular microscope bears the J. Swift & Son name and the serial 16616 on the back. The catalogue also records its Sedgwick Museum Cambridge mark and one fitted objective.
limits: The physical number identifies the body. The catalogue gives no date or Antarctic journey for this instrument.
alt: A dark monocular stand with brass trim, a mirror and a small eyepiece.

title: Swift microscope case labelled 30607
dateKind: The fitted case’s plate gives a serial, which is separate from an object date.
summary: The box label gives 30607. The institute records that the box was used with the older microscope numbered 16616. The lid keeps the number of its earlier instrument with adjusted lens identifiers.
limits: This case was reused. Its outer assignment and its present contents can both carry real records without identifying one common factory set.
alt: A tall wooden box with leather handle, green lining and a label visible inside the door.

title: Heath sextant case and August certificate
dateKind: Date of the examination certificate attached to the case.
summary: The case attached to the Heath sextant has a certificate dated August 1914. The catalogue relates the sextant to Frank Worsley’s later voyage aboard James Caird.
limits: The certificate dates an examination. It does not date a particular sighting or measure the instrument’s later accuracy.
alt: A low hinged box with a pale certificate sheet inside its lid.

title: Sextant with a June 1908 certificate
dateKind: Date of the examination certificate for this separate sextant.
summary: The museum records its distinct wooden case, four spare telescopes, spare lens and level. Its National Physical Laboratory certificate is dated June 1908.
limits: The same kind of certificate does not make this instrument Worsley’s Heath sextant. The date belongs to the certificate inside this case.
alt: A metal arc with an index arm, and a small pale rectangle for the certificate.

title: Worsley’s James Caird stopwatch
dateKind: Year of the boat journey on which the stopwatch is documented in use.
summary: The catalogue records Worsley’s use of this stopwatch with a sextant on the 1916 journey from Elephant Island to South Georgia. The face has a seconds scale and a smaller separate dial.
limits: Its use date does not tell when it was manufactured. The surviving watch does not give the time of a particular sighting.
alt: A pale round face with a blue hand, subdial and small top loop.

title: Scott’s canvas notebook wallet
dateKind: Retrieval by the search party. The institute records earlier use on the South Pole journey.
summary: The institute records this beige notebook wallet as used by Robert Falcon Scott on the South Pole journey and brought back by the search party in 1912.
limits: The retrieval year is not the making date. The wallet does not identify the contents of a missing notebook page.
alt: A folded beige canvas wallet with broken dark button and small belt loops.

title: Two paper pieces recovered from a Nimrod tent
dateKind: Field collection date. The tent’s Nimrod use preceded its later retrieval.
summary: The institute records a food-tin label and a coupon for a print. The Terra Nova expedition recovered them from an earlier Nimrod party tent on the Barrier.
limits: These fragments show objects saved there. The coupon is a separate printed item and does not describe what the party ate.
alt: One yellow scrap with a red border and a smaller white coupon with a yellow circle.

title: Cary dial barometer attributed to a Nimrod ascent
dateKind: The catalogue’s field date. Its account of use on the Erebus ascent is qualified.
summary: The institute describes a Cary aneroid barometer with a single steel pointer, a silvered dial and detachable scale magnifier. It says Edgeworth David reputedly used it on the first ascent of Mount Erebus.
limits: A dial can be read at one moment. The object and its qualified use history do not provide a time series from an ascent.
alt: A broad silver face with a dark pointer and small separate magnifier on a loop.

title: Fitted brown case with a 1907 mark
dateKind: Date stamped on this leather case. The associated use on Erebus is reputed.
summary: The fitted leather case for the Cary barometer has a buckle and velvet lining. Its stamp names the British Antarctic Expedition and gives 1907.
limits: The stamp links the case with an expedition. The case itself preserves no barometer reading.
alt: A six-sided brown case with curved lid and purple lining under its buckle.

title: Cary seven-day barograph
dateKind: Dates of the Nimrod expedition with which the instrument is reputedly associated.
summary: The institute describes a seven-day Cary barograph in a glazed wooden carrying case. It records a mechanical tracing arrangement and an expedition inscription on the case.
limits: A mechanism capable of drawing a trace is evidence of a recording method. This entry supplies no particular finished chart from that expedition.
alt: A glazed box showing a low drum shape and a marking arm.

title: Barograph’s spare ink bottle
dateKind: Date of the expedition with which the paired barograph is reputedly associated.
summary: The institute records a spare glass ink bottle for Y: 2024/6a. The bottle has purple ink residue and a stopper.
limits: Residue and a catalogue association tell what was carried with the barograph. They do not show the time or values on any chart.
alt: A squat stoppered glass vessel with a purple mark low on the side.

title: Sledge wheel taken south by Mawson
dateKind: BANZARE expedition that took this wheel. The earlier Terra Nova dates describe the type.
summary: The institute describes the wheel as a type used by Terra Nova and this wheel as taken to Antarctica by Douglas Mawson during BANZARE. It records a studded rim and revolution counter.
limits: Type history does not prove this wheel was present on Terra Nova. The counter does not provide a distance for a specific trip.
alt: A spoked wheel on a dark fork, with a small disc at the hub.

title: Terra Nova sledging biscuit under glass
dateKind: Expedition for which the biscuit formula was prepared.
summary: The collection describes a stamped rectangular biscuit in a tin with a glass front. It records a formula developed by Huntley & Palmers and Edward Wilson for use on Terra Nova.
limits: An intended use is evidence about preparation. This particular biscuit supplies no consumption or departure tally.
alt: A square dark tin with a pale perforated rectangle visible under glass.

title: Empty 2013 expedition-biscuit packet
dateKind: Date of the recreated biscuit product, over a century after Terra Nova.
summary: The collection records an empty cardboard packet for a product made in 2013 by Huntley & Palmers. The makers used a recreation of the earlier recipe with a change in fat.
limits: Packaging and an adapted recipe can show a later interpretation. This empty packet was not a supply carried on Terra Nova.
alt: A dark rectangular packet with a pale label and small separate barcode block.

title: Edward Nelson’s sounding sledge model
dateKind: Date of the expedition using the type shown in the model.
summary: The institute attributes this model to Terra Nova biologist Edward Nelson. It depicts a sounding and trawling sledge with a removable roll of rope, wire and boxes.
limits: The model records an arrangement. It does not establish the mass or performance of a full-size loaded sledge.
alt: Two miniature runners carrying a coil of line and two shapes for boxes.

title: Printed bird-recording forms for Penola
dateKind: Expedition for which the printed forms were prepared.
summary: The sheets were prepared to record observations of birds at sea on the British Graham Land Expedition.
limits: The existence of a recording form says how people meant to collect information. It does not show a particular sighting.
alt: A short stack of ruled sheets with blank entry spaces and a top clip.

title: Lister’s box of wrapped snowflake slide sets
dateKind: Field date given within the 1955–1958 Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition.
summary: The SPRI record describes a reused cigar box with a handwritten lid note and six paper bundles. The group is associated with Hal Lister’s field collection.
limits: Six describes packages. It does not count slides or estimate how much snow fell.
alt: A flat cardboard box with a handwritten note strip and six small package marks.

title: Snowflake impressions, set 1 · Y: 2022/9/2
dateKind: Field date given within the 1955–1958 Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition.
summary: The institute records 7 glass slides with snowflake impressions in resin under this accession. The catalogue describes a crêpe paper wrapper. It gives Hal Lister and 1955 in the field collection record.
limits: A count is for slides in this accession. It does not count distinct weather events, and the wrapper alone does not set the sampling location.
alt: A paper-wrapped set and a drawn slide. Its label gives 7 slides for this record.

alt: A paper-wrapped set and a drawn slide. Its label gives 5 slides for this record. A second tab names the institute on the wrapper.

title: Terra Nova signal flag from Hut Point
dateKind: Expedition on which the catalogue records the flag’s signal use.
summary: The institute identifies this flag as flown at Hut Point as a signal to Cape Evans. A bamboo pole fitted a sleeve at one edge.
limits: A record of a signal sent does not establish which person received it, when they saw it or how they acted.
alt: A folded red and blue flag edge against its long pale sleeve and bamboo.

title: Wilson’s Discovery sun compass
dateKind: Discovery expedition’s documented use on the southern sledge journey.
summary: The institute attributes the compass to E. A. Wilson. It records a wooden disc with handle and separate ink and pencil markings. The centre pin is missing.
limits: The surviving disc keeps some of the setup. It does not reproduce a recorded direction or a complete instrument as worked then.
alt: A small handled circular board, faded edge marks and empty centre.

title: Terra Nova sun compass marked Cape Evans
dateKind: Catalogue gives the Terra Nova use period. “Dec 1st” is a marking on the disc.
summary: The wooden compass carries a paper disc marked Cape Evans, latitude 78° south and December 1. The museum records its lost centre pin.
limits: The place, latitude and day on the disc concern this instrument’s reference. They do not show that it works with the same reading at any place.
alt: A dark-handled round board with two half-day sectors and separate Cape Evans label.

title: Discovery folding mica lantern
dateKind: Discovery expedition use recorded for the lantern.
summary: The record describes a folding metal lantern with mica panels and a reflective back. It explicitly links a separate leather case, N: 133b.
limits: The described light openings do not establish a particular receiver’s viewing position or any message the lantern conveyed.
alt: A tall gold-lit folding lantern with a darker panel on one side.

title: Discovery leather case for the mica lantern
dateKind: Expedition use recorded for the linked lantern and case.
summary: A separate catalogue records the worn black leather case as belonging to N: 133a. It records a flap, eyelet, metal catch and textile lining.
limits: The carrier case supports the association of the two objects. The case supplies no evidence about the brightness of a light.
alt: A dark leather folded case with a pale catch and stitch marks.

title: Penola automatic tide gauge
dateKind: British Graham Land Expedition’s documented use of the gauge.
summary: The institute describes the instrument as recording vertical movement of sea ice with the tide, using a pen in a wooden box. It names the British Graham Land Expedition.
limits: The gauge reflects the method used for this observation. It supplies no individual tide height and records no sample-water properties.
alt: A closed wood gauge box beside a schematic line pointing to a recording pen.

title: Kilner water-sample bottle
dateKind: The description dates the type as commonly used in 1939. The attached label says 1930–40.
summary: The clear bottle has a ceramic top and metal catch. The catalogue describes it as a type in common use by British polar expeditions in 1939.
limits: The type of bottle says how a sample might be held. Its record gives no collection site, sample result or date of filling this bottle.
alt: A clear straight-sided bottle with tall pale lid and a separate dark catch.
